questions.q: The maximum amount of share capital a company is permitted to issue according to its Memorandum of Association is known as the...
questions.explain: **Authorized Capital** (also called Registered or Nominal capital) is the maximum total value of shares that a company is legally permitted to issue to the public, as stated in its Memorandum of Association.

questions.q: Capital that is easily converted into cash or continuously changes its form during the normal course of business operations is termed...
questions.explain: **Circulating (or liquid) capital** refers to assets that change form constantly in the day-to-day running of the business. For example, cash is used to buy stock (inventory), stock is sold on credit to become debtors, and debtors pay up to become cash again.

questions.q: Which of the following is a widely used commercial instrument of credit that allows a buyer to defer payment for goods until a specified future date?
questions.explain: A **bill of exchange** is a vital instrument of credit in commerce. It is an unconditional order in writing, requiring the person to whom it is addressed to pay a specific sum of money on demand or at a fixed future date, thereby allowing for deferred payment.

questions.q: A business has total fixed assets of $\text{₦}500,000$, current assets of $\text{₦}150,000$, and current liabilities of $\text{₦}40,000$. What is the working capital of the business?
questions.explain:
Working capital is the excess of current assets over current liabilities. It represents the funds available for the day-to-day running of the business.

$$\text{Working Capital} = \text{Current Assets} - \text{Current Liabilities}$$
$$\text{Working Capital} = \text{₦}150,000 - \text{₦}40,000 = \text{₦}110,000$$

questions.q: Working capital is highly essential to a business enterprise primarily because it is used to...
options: purchase long-term fixed assets like land and machinery.
pay annual dividends to long-term shareholders.
meet the day-to-day financial obligations and operating expenses.
legally increase the authorized share capital of the company.
questions.explain: The **importance of working capital** lies in its use for the day-to-day financial operations of the business. It is used to pay for recurrent operational expenses like staff salaries, utility bills, and purchasing raw materials to keep the business running smoothly.

questions.q: In a commercial business, gross profit is best defined as the...
options: excess of total sales revenue over the cost of goods sold.
difference between total revenue and all operating expenses.
amount of capital originally invested by the entrepreneur.
net surplus declared by management after paying government taxes.
questions.explain: **Gross Profit** is strictly the trading profit. It is calculated by subtracting the cost of goods sold from the net sales revenue, before any general operating expenses (like rent or salaries) are deducted.
questions.exam: NECO Commerce Part 1: Introduction, Production & Trade Fundamentals

questions.q: If a trading firm records a gross profit of $\text{₦}120,000$, and incurs operating expenses consisting of salaries ($\text{₦}30,000$) and office rent ($\text{₦}15,000$), calculate the net profit.
questions.explain:
Net Profit is calculated by deducting total operating expenses from the Gross Profit.

$$\text{Total Expenses} = \text{Salaries} + \text{Rent}$$
$$\text{Total Expenses} = \text{₦}30,000 + \text{₦}15,000 = \text{₦}45,000$$

$$\text{Net Profit} = \text{Gross Profit} - \text{Total Expenses}$$
$$\text{Net Profit} = \text{₦}120,000 - \text{₦}45,000 = \text{₦}75,000$$

questions.q: During a trading year, a retailer had cash sales of $\text{₦}400,000$, credit sales of $\text{₦}250,000$, and customers returned goods worth $\text{₦}30,000$. Calculate the business turnover for the year.
questions.explain:
**Turnover** is defined as the net sales of a business during a specific period. It is calculated by adding cash and credit sales, then subtracting any returns inwards (sales returns).

$$\text{Total Sales} = \text{₦}400,000 + \text{₦}250,000 = \text{₦}650,000$$
$$\text{Turnover} = \text{Total Sales} - \text{Returns Inwards}$$
$$\text{Turnover} = \text{₦}650,000 - \text{₦}30,000 = \text{₦}620,000$$

questions.q: Which of the following factors is most likely to cause a rapid increase in the turnover of a retail business?
options: A sudden and steep increase in the unit price of goods.
A massive reduction in the firm's advertising budget.
The introduction of favorable credit facilities for reliable customers.
A persistently high rate of employee absenteeism.
questions.explain: Factors that positively affect turnover (boost sales) include aggressive advertising, competitive pricing, high demand, and allowing customers to buy on credit. **Introducing favorable credit facilities** encourages customers to buy more goods immediately, thereby increasing the business turnover.
